hints: Focus on what actually happens when each Period 3 chloride meets water, dissolving versus reacting to hydrolyse.
Remember that $\text{NaCl}$ just hydrates to ions with pH 7, while $\text{SiCl}_4$ and $\text{PCl}_5$ hydrolyse to give acidic $\text{HCl}$ solutions.
Think about which hydrolysis product mixture contains free mobile ions from strong acids, so the final solution can carry a current.
walkthrough:
**Sort the chlorides by bonding type**

Think of the trend across Period 3. $\text{NaCl}$ is truly ionic, $\text{AlCl}_3$ is intermediate with high polarising $\text{Al}^{3+}$, while $\text{SiCl}_4$ and $\text{PCl}_5$ are simple covalent molecules.

Bonding summary:
$$\text{NaCl: ionic} \quad \text{AlCl}_3: \text{covalent dimer Al}_2\text{Cl}_6 \quad \text{SiCl}_4, \text{PCl}_5: \text{covalent molecular}$$

**Compare dissolving and hydrolysing**

Dissolving is just separation into hydrated ions with no new bonds broken in water. Hydrolysis is a chemical reaction with water that makes $\text{HCl}$ plus an oxide or oxoacid.

$$\text{NaCl(s)} \rightarrow \text{Na}^{+}(\text{aq}) + \text{Cl}^{-}(\text{aq}) \text{ (no reaction, pH = 7)}$$

**Write the hydrolysis reactions**

$\text{SiCl}_4$ reacts vigorously despite strong $\text{Si-Cl}$ bonds because Si can accept a lone pair from water. $\text{PCl}_5$ does the same to give phosphoric acid and hydrochloric acid.

$$\text{SiCl}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{SiO}_2 + 4\text{HCl}$$
$$\text{PCl}_5 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 5\text{HCl}$$

**Link products to conductivity**

$\text{HCl}$ is a strong acid and $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ is a weak acid, so the $\text{PCl}_5$ mixture contains $\text{H}^{+}$, $\text{Cl}^{-}$ and phosphate ions. Mobile ions in solution mean it conducts electricity, so only that statement is correct.

options.A: Incorrect. Solid $\text{AlCl}_3$ is not a giant ionic lattice. The very small, highly charged $\text{Al}^{3+}$ strongly polarises $\text{Cl}^{-}$, so it exists as covalent $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$ dimers with bridging chlorides.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{NaCl}$ only undergoes physical dissolving and hydration to $\text{Na}^{+}(\text{aq})$ and $\text{Cl}^{-}(\text{aq})$. No $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{NaOH}$ are formed, and the solution stays neutral at pH 7.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{SiCl}_4$ hydrolyses vigorously with fumes of $\text{HCl}$ despite strong $\text{Si-Cl}$ bonds. Reaction occurs because Si has empty 3d orbitals and can expand its octet to accept a lone pair from water in the first step.
options.D: Correct. $\text{PCl}_5$ hydrolyses completely: $\text{PCl}_5 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 5\text{HCl}$. Both acids release mobile $\text{H}^{+}$, $\text{Cl}^{-}$ and other ions in water, so the resulting acidic solution conducts electricity well.
